No, the pedestrian will not prevail, because the adjuster's statement caused him no monetary loss: he rejected the $1,000 offer, hired counsel, and later won a $550,000 verdict, so he neither relied on the misstatement nor was damaged by it. The lack of a fiduciary relationship is not the controlling reason, since misrepresentation turns on reliance and loss rather than on a duty of loyalty. This is the second of the two options in the team note.

CONFIDENCE: 85
